subject: Hosted API commit ceiling increase & aggregated-rate proposal
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Turner <alyssa@parcelforge.io>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API commit ceiling increase & aggregated-rate proposal

Hi Alyssa —

Thanks again for the time this morning. As discussed, ParcelForge is seeing sustained traffic growth on your recommendations pipeline and we think a structured monthly commit increase will give you predictable capacity and lower unit cost. I attached a starter proposal (redwood_commit_proposal_v1.xlsx). High level: 

- New monthly commit: 15M generation tokens (up from 6M)
- Billing tiers: blended rate with a 3-month staircase (10M / 13M / 15M) to smooth spend
- Soft-rate smoothing: temporary 1.25x graceband on peak days for two quarters
- Ops: optional burst credits you can consume during Black Friday / product launches

Can you confirm whether procurement or finance should own the contract review? If you prefer, I can loop in our contracts specialist for a clean tracked redline. Key ask from ParcelForge: ensure the peak-rate fallback doesn’t throttle critical Redis-backed re-rankers.

Next steps I propose: benchmark week after signature, then a 30-day operational ramp. If this looks reasonable I can send a tracked contract and DocuSign link.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachment: redwood_commit_proposal_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Alyssa Turner <alyssa@parcelforge.io>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: ParcelForge Procurement <procurement@parcelforge.io>, Ethan Ross <ethan.ross@parcelforge.io>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API commit ceiling increase & aggregated-rate proposal

Karthik —

Thanks for the clear proposal and the quick follow-up. A few quick items from our side: 

1) Procurement will own contract review (looped).
2) We like the staircase approach but need a guaranteed soft fall-back so our devs aren’t rate-limited during mid-month spikes — especially on re-rank endpoints.
3) Can you clarify how the blended rate is calculated across tiers and whether unused commit rolls forward? Finance asked about roll-forward within a 3-month window.

Also: our compliance team will need the audit-log retention and region residency text in the SOW. Can you include a short clause?

If you can send a revised sheet that shows monthly spend projections and an explicit fallback behavior (and the SOW clause), Procurement can do an initial pass. Thanks — I can review and route internally tomorrow.

Best,
Alyssa Turner
Head of Platform Engineering | ParcelForge
alyssa@parcelforge.io

Ben / Monica — forwarding ParcelForge's reply (below). Highlights: they want explicit fallback behavior for re-rank endpoints, query about roll-forward rules, and compliance clause for audit/log retention.

Questions for ops: can we offer a negotiated soft-fallback lane that prevents token-level throttling for specific routes (re-rank/*) while still preserving overall commit consumption? If we expose a per-route soft-limit with automatic fallback to a cheaper compatible model, will that meet their needs?

If ops can draft a short paragraph to include in the SOW on region residency and retention, I can add it to the sheet and send a tracked contract. Customer wants numbers and a DocuSign link fast.

Thanks — Karthik

Subject: Re: Hosted API commit ceiling increase & aggregated-rate proposal

Karthik / Ben —

Quick ops read: we can support a per-route soft-fallback for re-rank endpoints with these constraints:

- Implementation: tag re-rank routes at the gateway and allocate a small reserved KV cache + a route-specific soft window.
- Behavior: when global commit consumption approaches 95%, route soft-window remains available for an extra 48 hours but will be metered to the committed rate (no silent throttling). After 48 hours, traffic falls back to the compatible model pool (one model down) until the next billing period or until manual override.
- Roll-forward: we do not natively roll unused commit forward, but we can offer a 3-month consumption smoothing credit (one-time, applied as token-credit) for up to 15% unused for the first renewal only.
- Compliance clause: "Audit logs retained for 13 months in the customer-selected region; access controls via customer KMS keys."

I'll attach a short ops note for the SOW and a simple capacity footprint (ops_capacity_note.pdf). If legal needs precise language we'll support the tracked redline.

-Monica
Director, Cloud Operations | Redwood Inference
monica@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Hosted API commit ceiling increase & aggregated-rate proposal

Alyssa —

Thanks for the quick internal routing. Per Monica's note I've updated the proposal to reflect: 

- Staircase commit over three months (10M / 13M / 15M) with monthly spend projections included in the revised attachment.
- Per-route soft-fallback for re-rank routes: reserved soft-window that extends 48 hours at metered consumption, followed by automatic model fallback.
- One-time 3-month smoothing credit: up to 15% of unused commit from the first renewal applied as token-credit.
- SOW clause: "Audit logs retained for 13 months in customer-selected region; integration with customer KMS for key management."

I've uploaded the updated sheet and a tracked contract to the HubSpot deal and attached the DocuSign envelope for signature: https://docusign.example.com/envelope/EF-12345. If Procurement signs the SOW we can schedule the ramp benchmark for the week after signature. 

Next steps: 
- Alyssa / Procurement: confirm redline comments by EOD Monday and sign if acceptable.
- Ops: schedule a 60-min runbook session after signature (Monica to own).

Appreciate the momentum — happy to hop on a short call if there are any remaining blockers.

Best,
Karthik
